title: Rotate Image
statement: You get a square grid of numbers. Turn it a quarter turn clockwise, so the left column becomes the top row, and do it inside the same grid. You may not build a second grid to copy into.

example.caption: The left column 1, 4, 7 (read bottom to top) becomes the top row 7, 4, 1.

idea.sentence: A clockwise turn is two simple flips: swap the grid across its main diagonal, then mirror every row.

jargon.plain: Swap rows and columns, so the cell at row i, column j trades places with row j, column i. The diagonal does not move.
Change the input grid itself and use only a few spare variables, not a second grid.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a square matrix of numbers, like [[1,2],[3,4]]. Every row needs n numbers.

vars.meaning: side length of the square grid, so the grid has n² cells

compare.bruteLabel: Copy every cell into a second grid
compare.optimalLabel: Swap and reverse inside the same grid

rows.name: Copy into a new grid
rows.note: Cell (r, c) goes to (c, n-1-r). Easy, but it needs a whole second grid, which the task forbids.

rows.name: Transpose, then reverse rows
rows.note: Each cell is touched about twice. Only a swap temporary is extra.

fast.takeaway: You must look at every cell, so n² is the floor. The prize is the space: O(1) instead of O(n²).

stages.title: Transpose
stages.note: For every pair above the diagonal, swap (i, j) with (j, i). Rows become columns.

stages.title: Reverse each row
stages.note: Mirror every row left to right. Together with the transpose this is exactly a clockwise quarter turn.

edges.title: One cell
edges.why: No pair to swap and a one-cell row mirrors to itself. Both loops simply do nothing.

edges.title: 2 by 2
edges.why: The smallest grid with a real swap. Only one pair (0,1) and (1,0) trades places.

edges.title: Start j at i + 1
edges.why: Let j run over the whole row and every pair is swapped twice, which undoes the transpose. Stay strictly above the diagonal.

edges.title: Odd size has a centre
edges.why: The middle cell sits on the diagonal and in the middle of its row, so both flips leave it alone.

gotchas.text: Mirror the rows only after the transpose. Reverse the rows first and then transpose, and you get a counter-clockwise turn instead.
Start the inner loop at i + 1. Starting at 0 swaps every pair twice and the grid ends up unchanged.
A swap line that begins with [ needs a leading semicolon, or the parser glues it onto the previous line as an index. Prettier writes ;[a, b] = [b, a].
Do not write matrix = newGrid. That only rebinds the local parameter, and the caller still sees the old, unrotated rows. Mutate the cells and rows you were given.
A [][]int is a slice of slices. Copying the outer slice shares every row, so a helper that wants to keep the original must copy each row. The driver here copies row by row before rotating.

recap.key: A clockwise quarter turn equals a transpose followed by reversing every row.
moves: Swap (i, j) with (j, i) for every j > i
Reverse the rows first, then transpose, to turn the other way
